paper_title: Are Large Language Models Really Good Logical Reasoners A Comprehensive   Evaluation and Beyond
caption: The evaluation matches between LLM judge and human annotations on the 300 samples.
model_annotation: This horizontal bar chart illustrates the percentage match between LLM judge annotations and human annotations across six categories for 300 samples, as presented in the paper "Are Large Language Models Really Good Logical Reasoners: A Comprehensive Evaluation and Beyond." The vertical axis lists the six categories in descending order of match percentage: "No Hallucination," "Oriented," "Active," "Self-aware," "Rigorous," and "Correct." The horizontal axis represents the percentage match, ranging from 0% to 100% in increments of 20%, with tick marks at 0%, 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, and 100%. Each category is represented by a single horizontal bar, divided into two segments: a solid blue segment labeled "Matched" and a light blue segment labeled "Not Matched" according to the legend. The "Matched" segment represents the percentage of samples correctly annotated by the LLM judge, while the "Not Matched" segment represents the percentage incorrectly annotated. The approximate values for the "Matched" segment are: "No Hallucination" at 98.33%, "Oriented" at 97.33%, "Active" at 97.00%, "Self-aware" at 94.00%, "Rigorous" at 95.33%, and "Correct" at 99.00%. The corresponding "Not Matched" segment values are: "No Hallucination" at 1.67%, "Oriented" at 2.67%, "Active" at 3.00%, "Self-aware" at 6.00%, "Rigorous" at 4.67%, and "Correct" at 1.00%. The bars are sorted in descending order based on the "Matched" percentage, with "Correct" having the highest match at 99.00% and "Self-aware" having the lowest match among the categories at 94.00%. The "Correct" category bar is fully blue, indicating 100% match, while the "No Hallucination" bar is the longest overall, indicating the highest total match percentage.
